    notes: "PipelineRoot._process P99 <= 0.5 ms including world_to_hud for 32 prompts and driver.frame dispatch (CameraSolver.solve <= 0.05 ms in the CAMERA_SOLVE stage; the frame_pre_draw handler is two assignments); RESCALING re-derivation <= 4 ms in one frame; container composite GPU <= 0.3 ms at 1080p, <= 1.0 ms at 2160p. DRAW-CALL TABLE (unit is draw calls, not ms; read per viewport with Viewport.get_render_info, which lags one frame in _process): D_world <= 350 (floor 4 + marks 20 + ysort 300 + caps 4 + fx 22; Failure and Trail D_FT_MAX 38 nested inside), D_root <= 63 chart closed (HUD 60 + hold 1 + filter 1 + container composite 1; probed: the composite is counted on the root; 62 expected with a null slot at MVP), <= 93 chart open (holds only because the HUD is hidden under a full-bleed plate; Chart Table D_L3 <= 40), D_world + D_root <= 1000; zoom-out steps: sum <= 1000 only plus the P99 frame ceilings, failing steps withheld via ZOOM_MIN_K. Render targets <= 3 MB (A) / 22 MB (B) at 1080p."
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"presentation_clock","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md   # under interfaces: contract presentation_clock; PipelineRoot reads tick_alpha, T, running, and the ADR-0001-amendment fields state and load_seq (state drives present_time; load_seq drives the camera CUT through the driver); no KernelStateView type"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"tick_alpha","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md   # under state_ownership: state tick_alpha; the CAMERA_SOLVE stage reads it only through PresentFrame.alpha (ADR-0009)"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"frame_order","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0008-render-pipeline-wiring-and-integer-scaling.md   # under api_decisions: purpose frame_order; PipelineRoot._process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION is the single PresentationHost; no PRESENTATION_LATE; the frame_pre_draw handler runs after all _process (probed)"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0009","items":[{"section":"interfaces","name":"presentation_facet","entry_yaml":"  - contract: presentation_facet
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: composition-root
    consumers:
      - presentation-subscribers
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    signal_signature: "PresentationFacet {views: PresentationViews, clock: PresentationClock, key_capacity: int, perception_access: bool (read-only; true only on the Perception Filter's facet and DIAGNOSTIC facets), subscribe(block_id: StringName, handler: Callable, subscriber_name: StringName) -> SubscriptionHandle}; class-bound wrapper around NotifyFacet (bound by the composition root at issue), lives in src/kernel/facets/; subscription is per block (ADR-0004); handler is a 2-argument method Callable (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken ending in return ctx.complete(); a PERCEPTION_OUT subscription without perception_access is refused with SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED (ADR-0004 check 6)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"interfaces","name":"presentation_stage_order","entry_yaml":"  - contract: presentation_stage_order
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: pipeline-root (PresentationDriver)
    consumers:
      - presenters
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    signal_signature: "PresentationStage PROJECT 0, CAMERA_SOLVE 1, AVATAR 2, FILTER 3, INSTRUMENTS 4, HUD 5, LIGHTING 6, TRAIL 7, AUDIO 8, DEBUG 9; PresentationDiscontinuity RESTORE 0, CAMERA_CUT 1; PresenterDescriptor {name, stage, reads: Array[int] (each strictly earlier), after: Array[StringName] (same-stage predecessors), present: Callable(frame: PresentFrame) -> void, on_discontinuity: Callable(kind: int) -> void; both standard method Callables of exactly one argument}; PresentationDriver.register / freeze (packed stage*1024+registration_index keys, Array.sort) / frame(host_delta, present_time) / notify_camera_cut; files in src/presentation/pipeline/"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"state_ownership","name":"present_frame","entry_yaml":"  - state: present_frame
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    owner_system: presentation-driver (PresentationDriver, hosted by PipelineRoot)
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    interface: "PresentFrame {alpha: float in [0, 1] read once per frame from PresentationClock, T: int, running: bool, present_time: float supplied by PipelineRoot (owner ADR-0008), present_delta: float, render_delta: float scaled by Engine.time_scale and clamped to DT_MAX}; one reused RefCounted; presentation-only, never a state block, never hashed or saved"
    write_access: presentation-driver-only
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"state_ownership","name":"load_seq","entry_yaml":"  - state: load_seq
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed; applied by the ADR-0001 amendment batch
    owner_system: kernel (TickDriver, exposed through PresentationClock)
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    interface: "PresentationClock.load_seq: int, read-only; +1 on every LOADING to RUNNING transition (restore, new game, cold load) immediately before deliver_all, never on PAUSED or SAVING to RUNNING; never hashed or saved; consumed only by PresentationDriver (and ADR-0008's camera CUT trigger)"
    write_access: kernel-only
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"sim_motion_interpolation","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: sim_motion_interpolation
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    api: "Placement.at(prev: Vector2i, curr: Vector2i, alpha: float) = per-axis floori(prev + (curr - prev) * alpha), written only through Placement.put (Node2D) or Placement.put_control (Control), with Placement.floor_v for derived integer offsets (parallax); alpha from PresentFrame; physics/common/physics_interpolation absent or false (asserted by effective value), SceneTree.physics_interpolation false, presentation roots Node.PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION_MODE_OFF, snap_2d_* flags as a safety net"
    not: "int(), round, roundi or truncation on a placement path; engine 2D physics interpolation; Tween or AnimationPlayer position/offset/transform tracks on sim-owned nodes; presenter-side previous/current caches; writing position, global_position, offset or transform by assignment, setter or relative-move method outside placement.gd and the named allow-list (viewport_wiring.gd, the camera host's frame_pre_draw handler)"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    reason: "One interpolator on one clock; Node2D has no get_global_transform_interpolated (probed 4.7.2) so an engine-interpolated pose is unreadable; floori is correct for negative coordinates; the kernel's prev/curr pair with snap_baseline survives restore and body transfer"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"presentation_render_callback","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: presentation_render_callback
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed; KRN-LAT-02 confirms the host order on a release export
    api: "PipelineRoot is the single PresentationHost: its one _process at ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION advances present_time, the zoom cooldown and the RESCALING re-derive, then calls PresentationDriver.frame(); presenters register Callables and define no _process; CameraSolver.solve runs in stage CAMERA_SOLVE; RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw only writes canvas_transform and the parallax offsets from the solved pose"
    not: "per-presenter _process nodes ordered by priority offsets or tree order; a second node doing presentation work at PRESENTATION; PRESENTATION_LATE; reading views or drawing inside a notification handler; presenters or the camera solve running in a frame_pre_draw handler"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    reason: "Order is a contract (HUD AC-HS-89, PF-35) and must be testable headless; the windowed 4.7.2 editor probe shows frame_pre_draw after every node _process, so a solve inside it would lag the HUD by a frame; one host node removes the priority-0 tie; release export, D3D12 and Deck remain UNVERIFIED (ADR-0008 spike steps 11 and 12)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"draw_or_read_in_notification_handler","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: draw_or_read_in_notification_handler
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "A subscriber, result or control-outcome handler only marks dirty (DirtyAccumulator.absorb), copies event scalars into a pre-sized ring and ends in return ctx.complete(); it never reads a view, touches a node, allocates, emits a signal, awaits (banned lexically in presenter and subscriber scripts) or submits."
    why: "Handlers run inside P5 with writes disabled and their cost is added to every other subscriber; views read there may be replaced by a later tick in the same frame; interpolation needs draws on frames with no notification."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"presentation_write_outside_allow_list","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: presentation_write_outside_allow_list
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Presentation writes only CanvasItem, Material, Light2D, LightOccluder2D, CanvasModulate, particle and audio members; never a block, a command, a physics body, Camera2D, Viewport, SubViewport, SubViewportContainer or CanvasLayer members (Pipeline root and camera host excepted), SceneTree.paused, Engine.time_scale or synthetic input; simulation code never names a presentation or Node-derived class."
    why: "Presentation never writes the simulation (kernel H4); a corruptible display must be a transform of presentation nodes only."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: engine_signal_in_kernel_or_sim
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed; consistent with ADR-0004 section 1 (kernel-owned observer registry, no engine signals)
    description: "No signal is declared or connected in src/kernel or src/sim; engine signals are used only between presentation objects for user-initiated events and never carry simulation values into a simulation module or replace a declared stage-read edge."
    why: "The simulation is scene-tree free and testable headless; signals are hidden synchronous dependencies that bypass the stage-read check."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"unrounded_or_foreign_placement","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: unrounded_or_foreign_placement
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "Position, global position, offset and transform of a Node2D or world-anchored Control (world layer 0, HUD layer 2) are written only in placement.gd (Placement.put / put_control) and the named allow-list (viewport_wiring.gd; the camera host's frame_pre_draw handler for canvas_transform and Placement.floor_v parallax offsets), by assignment, setter, relative-move method or animation property track; sim-owned positions are never rounded with int(), round or roundi and never animated by Tween or AnimationPlayer; presenters read alpha only from PresentFrame (tick_alpha is read only in presentation_driver.gd). Layer 3 and 4 UI Controls are outside the pattern."
    why: "One floor function and one alpha per frame keep the camera, the beam chest point and the sprite on the same pixel at every render rate."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: presentation_state_fed_back_or_persisted
    status: active           # ADR-0009 is Proposed
    description: "A presentation-local scalar is never persisted, hashed, replicated or read by the simulation, never decides visibility of a truth-channel element, never changes what a value settles to, and is reset by on_discontinuity on restore, new game, camera cut and hard_start."
    why: "Restore must need no special draw path and a truth channel must stay a pure reader of the simulation."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"revise_existing","name":"presentation_clock","entry_yaml":"  - contract: presentation_clock
    status: active
    pattern: direct_call
    producer: command-simulation-layer (TickDriver)
    consumers:
      - presentation-subscribers
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
    signal_signature: "PresentationClock.tick_alpha: float; PresentationClock.T: int; PresentationClock.running: bool; PresentationClock.state: int (KernelState enum); PresentationClock.load_seq: int (+1 on every LOADING to RUNNING, immediately before deliver_all; never on PAUSED/SAVING to RUNNING); all read-only, never hashed or saved"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: "2026-10-28 (ADR-0009 request, TD-04: state and load_seq)""},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"presentation_submit_without_handle","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md   # boot check ties SurfaceHandle names (issue_surface_handle) to INPUT_SURFACE registrations; submit-site list is ADR-0002's"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md   # PresentFrame.present_time is the only cosmetic clock; T only for values the sim also computes"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"kernel_autoload_or_global","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md   # presentation receives PresentationFacet through setup()"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"tick_alpha","entry_yaml":"    referenced_by (add):
      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md   # read once per frame into PresentFrame.alpha, only in presentation_driver.gd"},{"section":"referenced_by_update","name":"owner_callable_contract","entry_yaml":"      - docs/architecture/adr-0009-presentation-subscriber-contract.md   # subscriber handlers are kernel-invoked callables (batch: ChangeBatch, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken ending return ctx.complete()"}]},{"adr":"ADR-0010","items":[{"section":"api_decisions","name":"source_layout","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: source_layout
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "Layer-first tree: src/shared (L0, imports nothing; scene-tree-free, I/O-free, no global state; IntMath and src/shared/det), src/kernel and src/data and src/save (L1; save is RefCounted only), src/sim/<system> for graph, layout, body, emitter, controller, interaction, suit, assembly, web, attention, horror, sanity (L2), src/presentation/<system> for pipeline, perception, lighting, trail, hud, instruments, chart, audio, controller, projector (L3; shared presentation files in pipeline/), src/game (composition root, KernelHost src/game/kernel_host.gd, SaveHost src/game/save_host.gd, MonotonicClock, SystemWallClock), src/debug and src/observer (dev only, guarded load); published surfaces are kernel/facets (the presentation-visible kernel API list), kernel/ports, sim/<x>/views, sim/<x>/ports; test seams only in src/<module>/testing/"
    not: "src/sanity/ or any module path outside src/sim/<system>/; PROJECTOR scripts under src/sim/; a scene or Node-derived script in shared, kernel, data, save or sim (SaveHost and KernelHost are Nodes and live in src/game); any script under src/ outside the listed directories; presentation naming a kernel class outside kernel/facets"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Makes simulation-never-reads-presentation, tree-freedom and warning scope directory tests, and resolves IC-10"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"presentation_visible_kernel_api","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: presentation_visible_kernel_api
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "Presentation, debug and observer code may name only these kernel classes, all under src/kernel/facets/: PresentationClock, SurfaceHandle, ControlHandle, ModuleFacet, BlockRegistrar, ChangeBatch, NotifyContext, CompletionToken, NotifyEvent, DirtyAccumulator, KeyBuf, NotifyFacet, SubscriptionHandle, SubscriberClass, DirtyKey, PresentationFacet, PresentationViews; NotifyFacet is named only by src/game and PresentationFacet; ARCH-08 denies Kernel, KernelHost, TickDriver, SimViews, WriteScope, Command, BlockDescriptor, CallContext, ValidateContext, ApplyContext, HookContext, SnapshotContext; the list is data in tools/lint/config/edges.json"
    not: "a *Context glob ban (NotifyContext is a legal facets type); KernelStateView (state is PresentationClock.state, the restore marker PresentationClock.load_seq); presentation holding NotifyFacet"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Presenter handlers must name NotifyContext and CompletionToken (ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0009); the deny list names only tick-phase types"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"interface_mechanism","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: interface_mechanism
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed; LINT-SPIKE-1(a) confirms @abstract survives a release export
    api: "@abstract base class (port) in the ports/ directory of the lowest layer every consumer may import (single-consumer ports listed as port_files); implementations and hand-written test doubles extend it and restate the full signature including the return type; consumers type setup() parameters as the port; REFLECT-SIG compares each argument's type, class_name and hint_string and the return type, class_name and hint_string"
    not: "an abstract BlockOwner for owner callables (ADR-0003 section 1 keeps registered Callables); IFoo names; duck-typed objects checked only by has_method; reflective GDScript.new() on a port; gdUnit4 mock() of a port unless LINT-SPIKE-1 proves it works; a plain push_error base class except as the documented fallback"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Probed 2026-10-28 on 4.7.2: a subclass missing an abstract method and a direct PortBase.new() are parse errors"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"gdscript_warning_policy","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: gdscript_warning_policy
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "project.godot [debug] gdscript/warnings/*: every severity 2 except RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED 0, none at 1; directory_rules {res://: 0, res://addons: 0, res://tests: 0, res://src: 1, res://tools: 1}; CI gate tools/ci/load_all.gd loads every src and tools script and fails on null, can_instantiate() false or a SCRIPT ERROR log line; every @warning_ignore, _start and _restore form in src and tools must be an entry of tools/lint/config/allowlists/warning_ignore.json (PRJ-04), whose only initial entry is integer_division in IntMath.trunc_div; promotion is verified on the editor binary, not on a release export"
    not: "warnings left at level 1 (invisible in a headless run); a second strictness tier for presentation; directory_rules decision values other than 0 and 1 (engine error); an @warning_ignore of any warning that is not on the allow-list; := in src or tools"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Probed 2026-10-28: severity is global per warning, directory_rules is include/exclude only, level-1 warnings print nothing headless"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"integer_division_site","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: integer_division_site
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "IntMath in src/shared/int_math.gd (function list and divisor guard owned by ADR-0005); the single @warning_ignore(\"integer_division\") in src/ sits on the return statement of IntMath.trunc_div; the operator tokens /, %, /= and %= are banned outright in shared, kernel and sim outside IntMath (SIM-04); over-range decimal literals are banned (SIM-15)"
    not: "a bare integer or vector / or % in shared, kernel or sim; min, max, clamp, abs, sign, floor, ceil, round, int(), float() or trig functions in those directories; a second integer_division ignore or a '# nn:' marker site"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Truncation toward zero and signed % probed on 4.7.2; INTEGER_DIVISION fires only for int / int, so Vector2i division, /= and % need the lexical rule; ADR-0005 section 1.4 and 1.7 adopt the same single site (OQ-L closed)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"lint_forbidden_token_list","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: lint_forbidden_token_list
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "One forbidden-token list for time and randomness, owned by ADR-0010 SIM-02: any Time. member; OS.get_ticks_*, OS.get_unix_time*, OS.delay_*; Engine.get_frames_*, get_physics_frames, get_process_frames; get_process_delta_time, get_physics_process_delta_time; randi, randf, randi_range, randf_range, randfn, randomize, seed(, rand_from_seed, RandomNumberGenerator, Crypto, pick_random, shuffle; allow-list exactly kernel_host.gd, the diagnostics timer, monotonic_clock.gd, system_wall_clock.gd; ADR-0001 and ADR-0005 point at it"
    not: "a second token list in another ADR; render-time timers using Time.* (they use delta, present_time or the injected Clock); wall time entering a block, a hash or an ordering decision"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Unions ADR-0005 section 1.7 and ADR-0001 entries so the lint has one owner"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"lint_tool_and_tiers","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: lint_tool_and_tiers
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "tools/lint/lint_main.gd (headless GDScript, extends SceneTree, OS.get_cmdline_user_args(), quit(0|1|2)) with core/ library and tools/lint/<pack>_lint.gd packs; one finding format LINT-<PACK>-<NN> <error|warn> <path>:<line>: <rule>: <message>; exit 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 tool failure (including a stale class map); tiers E1 engine parser, E2 lexical scan, E3 reflection, E4 runtime counters and boot walks; every rule has bad and good fixtures under tests/fixtures/lint/<rule>/ and a '# lint-allow: RULE reason' waiver unless marked no-waiver; run by CLI before gdUnit4 and by per-system wrappers tests/unit/<system>/lint/; MVP minimum rule set required at KRN-LAT-02"
    not: "gdtoolkit or any Python parser as a blocking gate; a rule stated as 'lint-enforced' without a rule id and tier; a lint that claims to see types, data flow or WriteScope membership; treating lint exit codes as kernel fault domains"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "GDScript has no public AST; reflection and the class map exist only in-engine; ADR-0007 already makes GDScript the CI tool language"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"allocation_verification","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: allocation_verification
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "zero-allocation acceptance wording = HOT-01 token scan of '## @hot' functions (transient allocation) + OBJECT_COUNT unchanged over 600 ticks + MEMORY_STATIC within tolerance over 600 ticks on the debug binary (retained growth) + is_same and is_read_only() on every array accessor + injected WorkCounter counts for algorithmic budgets; accessors return Array[T] or Dictionary[K, V] marked read-only, never a Packed*Array; Kernel.dispose() leaves no reference cycle (weakref back-references, no stored capturing lambdas)"
    not: "claiming 'zero heap allocations' from OBJECT_COUNT alone (arrays, dictionaries, strings and lambdas add 0); using == for identity; conditional compilation flags for counters; MEMORY_STATIC or MEMORY_STATIC_MAX as a per-window or release-build gate; exposing a Packed*Array from an accessor"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "Probed 2026-10-28: OBJECT_COUNT blind to arrays; MEMORY_STATIC sees retained (1.7 MB) but not transient (208 B for 100k) allocation; packed arrays have no read-only marker"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"test_framework_pin","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: test_framework_pin
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed; LINT-SPIKE-1(g) re-observes it
    api: "gdUnit4 6.2.2 committed under addons/gdUnit4 against Godot 4.7.2; lane H headless runs exactly the project.yaml commands.test string (tests/unit, tests/integration), lane W windowed (tests/render only), lane P nightly release-export benchmark; exit 101 (leaked nodes) counts as failure; render suites never run in lane H and are listed SKIPPED; unlisted engine ERROR or WARNING log lines fail lane H; --import retried up to three times or .godot cached; port doubles are hand-written, not mock()"
    not: "changing the gdUnit4 version without repeating the spike; a render-tagged check that can pass headless or with a zero draw count; treating 'No test cases found' as a pass"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "6.2.2 observed running on 4.7.2 (current-best-practices.md, 2026-10-17); the gdUnit4 README lists 4.7.1 at most"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"native_code_policy","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: native_code_policy
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "GDScript only through MVP; ladder rung 0 as written, rung 1 tuning, rung 2 call-overhead removal, rung 3 GDExtension only for the Graph propagate phases after Spike S1 / SP-ENG-1 evidence on RM-DECK and an accepted ADR amendment; the port stays a GDScript @abstract class, the extension registers a plain RefCounted-derived native class and a GDScript adapter extends the port and forwards calls; the GDScript implementation stays as golden reference, both run the full suite and replay state_hash in CI; integer-only API, no Node, no threads, built with -fwrapv, Windows and Linux x86_64"
    not: "C# (the mono editor is not the shipping runtime); GDExtension for presentation or Node-bound code; a native class that is expected to satisfy `is Port`; native code before S1 evidence; selecting the implementation by a global flag read inside the simulation"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "A GDExtension class can extend only a native class, so the adapter is the only way to keep one seam and unchanged call sites"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"api_decisions","name":"wall_clock_port","entry_yaml":"  - purpose: wall_clock_port
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    api: "WallClock (@abstract, src/save/wall_clock.gd, now_unix() -> int) is the only wall-time source; implemented by src/game/system_wall_clock.gd (the fourth SIM-02 allow-list entry); injected only into SaveService.setup(); created_unix and SaveInfo time are display metadata and never an ordering, gate or hash input"
    not: "a Time.* token outside the SIM-02 allow-list; a wall-clock value in a block, hash or ordering decision; the port living in src/kernel; a render-timer exemption"
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    reason: "ADR-0006 needs a header timestamp; the monotonic Clock port cannot supply it (TD-11)"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"interfaces","name":"wall_clock","entry_yaml":"  - contract: wall_clock
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    pattern: direct_call     # injected port (setup parameter)
    producer: system-wall-clock   # src/game/system_wall_clock.gd
    consumers:
      - save-load-service        # SaveService.setup() only
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    signal_signature: "WallClock.now_unix() -> int"
    referenced_by:
      - docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28
    revised: """},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"preload_or_load_of_script_in_src","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: preload_or_load_of_script_in_src
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    description: "No preload, load or ResourceLoader of a .gd path anywhere in src/ (reference other systems by class_name); non-script preload only in src/presentation and src/game; the one guarded load() of the dev roots in src/game is the sole exception. No waiver (ARCH-03)."
    why: "Architecture dependency rule 2: a preload cycle fails to parse and hides coupling; the import-edge matrix is checked on class_name tokens."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"scene_tree_or_engine_server_in_sim_layers","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: scene_tree_or_engine_server_in_sim_layers
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    description: "No Node-derived class, scene-tree token (Node, SceneTree, get_tree, get_node, $, @onready, @export, _process, _input), engine server (RenderingServer, PhysicsServer2D, AudioServer, DisplayServer) or Input singleton in src/shared, src/kernel, src/data, src/save or src/sim. KernelHost and SaveHost live in src/game. No waiver (SIM-01)."
    why: "Kernel H10 and architecture Principle 1: the simulation runs headless; gdUnit4 runs inside a tree so tree-freedom is a lint, not an arrangement."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"float_or_wall_clock_in_sim","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: float_or_wall_clock_in_sim
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    description: "No float declaration, float literal, float-producing member (.length, .normalized, .distance_to, ...), Vector2/Vector3/Transform2D, or any SIM-02 token (Time.*, Engine frame counters, get_process_delta_time, global RNG) in src/shared and src/sim; kernel and data confine floats and clock reads to the float allow-list (presentation_clock.gd, the diagnostics timer, *_read.gd) and the four-entry SIM-02 allow-list; the src/shared float allow-list is exactly det_rng_float.gd and canonical_encoder.gd."
    why: "Kernel H9, determinism by construction; a float or a wall-clock read that reaches state breaks replay and the state hash."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md
    added: 2026-10-28"},{"section":"forbidden_patterns","name":"integer_division_outside_int_math","entry_yaml":"  - pattern: integer_division_outside_int_math
    status: active           # ADR-0010 is Proposed
    description: "The operator tokens /, %, /= and %= appear only inside IntMath in shared, kernel and sim; there is exactly one @warning_ignore(\"integer_division\") in src/, on IntMath.trunc_div; min, max, clamp, abs, sign, floor, ceil, round and trig functions are not used on simulation values (use mini, maxi, clampi, absi, signi)."
    why: "Negative operands truncate toward zero and % keeps the sign (probed on 4.7.2); Vector2i division truncates silently and escapes INTEGER_DIVISION; one tested site removes the class of off-by-one bugs."
    adr: docs/architecture/adr-0010-source-layout-static-typing-and-lint-enforcement.md

attachment.content:
- adopt: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.
- agents-sdk: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Agents SDK applications using the agents package.
- architecture-decision: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.
- architecture-review: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.
- art-bible: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.
- asset-audit: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.
- asset-spec: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.
- balance-check: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.
- basin: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare Basin analytics workflows with Basin Pipelines, Basin Catalog, and Basin SQL. Use for streaming data into R2 Iceberg tables, managing catalogs, or querying those tables; also use for requests using the former Data Platform, Pipelines, R2 Data Catalog, or R2 SQL names.
- brainstorm: Guided concept ideation using professional studio techniques, player psychology, creative exploration.
- brownfield: First-principles audit and improvement plan for an EXISTING codebase ("brownfield" project) — especially one the user can run and demo but can't confidently judge. Orchestrates parallel specialist subagents (architecture, product-intent, code, tests, security, performance, docs) that treat existing code as evidence rather than ground truth, keeps an assumptions register and escalates the risky ones, writes a consolidated improvement design doc with a dependency-ordered PR plan sized to the repo, runs a writer↔reviewer loop until no critical/major issues remain, and optionally (--execute) implements the plan as worktree-isolated, reviewed git branches. Use this skill whenever the user says /brownfield, asks to audit / health-check / assess / sanity-check / "second opinion" an existing repo or legacy app, asks "is this built correctly?", "what's wrong with this codebase?", "a contractor/AI built this and I'm not sure it's right", wants a prioritized improvement or remediation plan for code that already exists, or is inheriting a project and wants to know where the bodies are buried — even if they never use the word "brownfield". Not for greenfield design of new systems or for reviewing a single small diff/PR.
- bug-report: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.
- bug-triage: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.
- ccgs-code-review: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.
- changelog: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.
- cloudflare: Discover and choose Cloudflare products for apps, APIs, AI agents, storage, networking, and security. Use for architecture and product selection, including when the user describes a need without naming a Cloudflare product; then find the relevant skill or documentation.
- cloudflare-email-service: Implement or troubleshoot Cloudflare Email Sending and Email Routing integrations and their delivery configuration.
- cloudflare-one: Design, configure, troubleshoot, or review Cloudflare One Zero Trust and SASE deployments. Use cloudflare-one-migrations for migration planning from other vendors.
- cloudflare-one-migrations: Assess and plan migrations from existing VPN, SWG, or SASE platforms to Cloudflare One, including policy mapping, parity gaps, and rollout.
- code-review: Review a branch, PR, commit range, or working tree with separate Standards and Spec tasks through review_run. Use when the user asks for a code review or asks to review changes since a fixed point.
- consistency-check: Scan GDDs against the entity registry for cross-document conflicts. Grep-first approach targets conflicting sections, different stats.
- content-audit: Audit GDD content counts against what's implemented — planned vs built.
- create-architecture: Author the architecture blueprint before code is written. Validates decisions against the pinned engine, flags knowledge gaps.
- create-control-manifest: Flat must-do/never-do rules sheet per system and layer, extracted from Accepted ADRs. ADRs explain why; this is actionable.
- create-epics: Turn GDDs plus architecture into epics — one per architectural module, with untraced requirements. Then /create-stories [epic-slug].
- create-stories: Break one epic into implementable stories embedding TR-ID, ADR guidance, acceptance criteria. Reads the control manifest. After /create-epics.
- design-review: Reviews one design document for completeness, internal consistency, implementability, and design standards. Before handing to programmers.
- design-system: Section-by-section GDD authoring for one system — walks through each required section, cross-references dependencies.
- durable-objects: Build, debug, or review Cloudflare Durable Objects code for persistent state and coordination.
- estimate: Estimate task effort from complexity, dependencies, velocity, risk. Structured estimate with confidence levels.
- gate-check: Ready to advance between development phases? PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL with blockers and required artifacts. 'Can we move to production?'
- help: What should I do next? Use when stuck or you don't know what to do.
- k2: Build and troubleshoot Cloudflare K2 or K2 Streams durable logs. Use for stream setup, producing from Workers or HTTP, configuring retention and inputs, and consuming through subscriptions.
- launch-checklist: Launch readiness across every department: code, content, store, marketing, community, infrastructure, legal, go/no-go sign-offs.
- legion: Route legion <command> requests to the Legion CLI for Claude Code.
- localize: Localization pipeline — find hardcoded strings, extract string tables, cultural review, VO, RTL, enforce string freeze.
- map-systems: Decompose a concept into individual systems, map dependencies, prioritize design order, create the systems index.
- milestone-review: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.
- nextjs-on-cloudflare: Build, migrate, and deploy Next.js apps on Cloudflare Workers with vinext. Use when starting a Next.js project on Cloudflare, moving an existing app to Workers, choosing between vinext and OpenNext, or setting up vinext for Workers. For setup, migration, or deployment, install vinext's upstream skills with `npx skills add cloudflare/vinext` if missing, then read and follow the applicable skill and docs.
- onboard: Onboarding doc for a new contributor or agent — project state, conventions, priorities relevant to the specified role.
- orchestrate-omp: Coordinate OMP subagents on substantial work. Use when parallel discovery, specialist review, or clearly partitioned implementation will shorten or strengthen the result; skip trivial tasks.
- patch-notes: Player-facing patch notes from git history and changelogs. Translates developer language into player communication.
- perf-profile: Performance profiling — find bottlenecks, measure against budgets, produce ranked optimization recommendations.
- playtest-report: Structured playtest report template, or turn existing playtest notes into structured feedback.
- project-stage-detect: Analyze project state, detect stage, identify gaps, recommend next steps. 'Where are we in development?'
- propagate-design-change: A GDD changed — scan ADRs and the traceability index for now-stale architectural decisions. Impact report, guides resolution.
- prototype: Concept prototype before GDDs — throwaway HTML, Engine or Paper build, PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL/NOT ASSESSED. After /brainstorm and /setup-engine.
- pstack-omp: OMP adapter for poteto-mode. Maps canonical pstack roles and lifecycle protocols to current OMP task agents, batching, isolation, IRC follow-ups, and durable result resources.
- qa-plan: QA test plan for a sprint — classifies stories by Logic/Integration/Visual/UI, covers automated tests, manual cases, smoke scope.
- quick-design: Lightweight spec for small changes — tuning adjustments, minor mechanics. Embeds directly into stories; skips full GDD.
- regression-suite: Map test coverage to GDD critical paths, find fixed bugs lacking regression tests, flag drift from new features.
- release-checklist: Pre-release checklist — build verification, certification requirements, store metadata, launch readiness.
- research: Research a question with high-trust primary sources and save cited findings. Use when the user requests research, documentation facts, or API facts.
- retrospective: Sprint or milestone retrospective from completed work, velocity, blockers. Actionable insights for the next iteration.
- reverse-document: Generate missing design or architecture docs from existing implementation — works backwards from code and prototypes.
- review-all-gdds: Holistic cross-GDD review — contradictions between systems, dominant strategies, economic imbalance, cognitive overload, pillar drift.
- sandbox-migrate-to-next: Migrate Cloudflare Sandbox apps from stable @cloudflare/sandbox to @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-next for apps already on the preview.
- sandbox-next: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on @cloudflare/sandbox@next (SDK 1.0 preview). Use sandbox-migrate-to-next when porting a stable app.
- sandbox-stable: Build or maintain Cloudflare Sandbox apps on the stable @cloudflare/sandbox package. Use sandbox-next for preview apps and sandbox-migrate-to-next for stable-to-preview migrations.
- scope-check: Scope creep check — current scope versus the original plan. Flags additions, quantifies bloat, recommends cuts. 'Any scope creep?'
- security-audit: Security audit — save tampering, cheat vectors, network exploits, data exposure, input validation. Before public or multiplayer release.
- settings: View or change project config — effective merged values, or set locally in project.local.yaml.

# Global instructions (all projects)

## Dynamic Workflows: model choice

- Always use Sonnet 5.5 (`model: 'sonnet'`) or Haiku (`model: 'haiku'`) for worker agents in Dynamic Workflows (the Workflow tool's `agent()` calls), to preserve token usage. Use Haiku for mechanical stages (logging, formatting, simple extraction) and Sonnet for the rest.
- Opus or Fable is acceptable only as an advisor where needed: a senior reviewer, judge or verdict seat, never for bulk work such as planners, writers, fixers or scanners.
- Set `model` explicitly on every worker `agent()` call; do not let workers inherit the session model.

# Claude Code Game Studios -- Game Studio Agent Architecture

Indie game development managed through 49 coordinated Claude Code subagents.
Each agent owns a specific domain, enforcing separation of concerns and quality.

## Technology Stack

- **Engine**: Godot 4.7.2
- **Language**: GDScript
- **Version Control**: Git with trunk-based development
- **Build System**: SCons (engine), Godot Export Templates
- **Asset Pipeline**: Godot Import System + custom resource pipeline

> **Note**: Engine-specialist agents exist for Godot, Unity, and Unreal with
> dedicated sub-specialists. Use the set matching your engine.

## Project Structure

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

## Engine Version Reference

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md


## Technical Preferences

`project.yaml` at the repo root is the primary config store — engine, specialists,
naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`
(see `.claude/docs/config-resolution.md`).

`.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` is the **legacy fallback**, read on demand
when a key is absent from `project.yaml`. It is not imported here: before
`/setup-engine` runs it is almost entirely `[TO BE CONFIGURED]` placeholders, and
after it runs `project.yaml` holds the real values.

## Coordination Rules

@.claude/docs/coordination-rules.md

## Collaboration Protocol

**User-driven collaboration, not autonomous execution.**
Every task follows: **Question -> Options -> Decision -> Draft -> Approval**

- Agents MUST ask "May I write this to [filepath]?" before using Write/Edit tools
  (exempt: `active.md` appends, agent memory, a subagent's new file at the path
  its orchestrating skill named; see `.claude/rules/agent-memory.md`)
- Agents MUST show drafts or summaries before requesting approval
- Multi-file changes require explicit approval for the full changeset
- No commits without user instruction
- A skipped or dismissed question is not an answer: act on nothing, re-ask in
  plain text and wait
- Started outside this file's folder? Warn first: hooks, deny rules and the
  ask-first mode load only when Claude Code starts here

See `docs/COLLABORATIVE-DESIGN-PRINCIPLE.md` for full protocol and examples.

> **First session?** If the project has no engine configured and no game concept,
> run `/start` to begin the guided onboarding flow.

## Coding Standards

@.claude/docs/coding-standards.md

## Context Management

Read `.claude/docs/context-management.md` on demand — it is a reference, not
session context. Two of its conventions are load-bearing and cited by name
elsewhere in the repo, so they are restated here rather than lost:

- **`production/session-state/active.md` is the session checkpoint.** The file is
  the memory, not the conversation. Read it first after any compaction, crash, or
  `/clear`.
- **Helpers in `.claude/scripts/` emit observations, never verdicts.** A script
  that scores or judges will eventually contradict a mode or override it cannot
  see. (Cited by `artifact-check.sh` and `adr-dep-graph.sh`.)

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

| **LLM Knowledge Cutoff** | May 2025 |

## Knowledge Gap Warning

The LLM's training data likely covers Godot up to ~4.3. Versions 4.5, 4.6
and 4.7 were released after the cutoff and introduced significant changes that
the model does NOT know about; 4.4 came out shortly before it and may be thinly
covered. Always cross-reference this directory before suggesting Godot API calls.

## Installed-Version Gap Warning

The warning above is one-directional — it covers the **model** knowing less than
this pin. The reverse gap is real and `/setup-engine` §3 creates it deliberately
("pin the newer one and upgrade later"): this reference can sit **ahead of the
installed editor**, and an agent citing it correctly then emits APIs that do not
compile locally. **Check `Installed at pin time` above before trusting a
version-qualified claim** — `NOT DETERMINED` means the gap is unknown, not absent.

## Post-Cutoff Version Timeline

| Version | Release | Risk Level | Key Theme |
|---------|---------|------------|-----------|
| 4.5 | Sep 2025 | HIGH | Accessibility (AccessKit), variadic args, @abstract, shader baker, SMAA |
| 4.6 | Jan 2026 | HIGH | Jolt default, glow rework, D3D12 default on Windows, IK restored |
| 4.7 | Jun 2026 | HIGH | AreaLight3D, HDR output, Asset Store replaces the Asset Library, VirtualJoystick, Jolt soft-body and world-boundary changes, typed-return overrides |

## Before the Cutoff

4.4 (Mar 2025, Jolt option, FileAccess return types) predates the May 2025
cutoff; the Knowledge Gap Warning still applies to it.

Dates from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases, checked 2026-10-17:
4.4 Mar 3 2025, 4.5 Sep 15 2025, 4.6 Jan 26 2026, 4.7 Jun 18 2026, 4.7.2 Aug 18
2026. Migration guides and release notes: `breaking-changes.md` § Sources.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,

@.claude/docs/directory-structure.md

@docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md

naming, platform, performance, modes. Skills resolve it via `resolve_config`

# Directory Structure

```text
/
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Master configuration
├── project.yaml                 # Machine-readable project config — engine, modes, stage (source of truth)
├── .claude/                     # Agent definitions, skills, hooks, rules, docs
├── <code root>/                 # Game source code — THE PATH IS ENGINE-SPECIFIC, see below
├── assets/                      # Game assets (art, audio, vfx, shaders, data)
├── design/                      # Game design documents (gdd, narrative, levels, balance)
├── docs/                        # Technical documentation (architecture, api, postmortems)
│   └── engine-reference/        # Curated engine API snapshots (version-pinned)
├── tests/                       # Game test suites (unit, integration, performance, playtest)
├── tools/                       # Build and pipeline tools (ci, build, asset-pipeline)
├── prototypes/                  # Throwaway prototypes (outside the code root)
├── production/                  # Production management (sprints, milestones, releases)
│   ├── session-state/           # Ephemeral session state (active.md — gitignored)
│   └── session-logs/            # Session audit trail (gitignored)
└── studio-tests/                # QA for the skills/agents themselves — /skill-test, /skill-improve
```

## The code root is engine-specific

**Two of the three supported engines will not build a project whose code sits in
`src/`.** This is not a style preference — it is a hard constraint of the engine's
own toolchain:

| `engine.name` | Code root | Why it cannot be `src/` |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `src/` | No constraint — Godot loads from `res://` anywhere under the project root. |
| **Unity** | `Assets/` | Unity compiles **only** `Assets/` and `Packages/`. Code outside them is invisible to the compiler. |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/` | UnrealBuildTool discovers modules under `Source/`; content lives in `Content/`. A module elsewhere is not built. |

**Resolve the code root from `engine.name` before writing any source file.** A
path shown as `src/…` alone is a Godot example: read it as *"the code root"* and
substitute the row above. `src/` is the table's Godot row, not a universal path.

**Tests follow the same rule** — the same compilers decide what they see:

| `engine.name` | Test root | Anywhere else |
|---|---|---|
| **Godot** | `tests/unit/`, `tests/integration/` | — |
| **Unity** | `Assets/Tests/EditMode/`, `Assets/Tests/PlayMode/` | not compiled: "0 tests, Passed" |
| **Unreal** | `Source/<Module>/Private/Tests/` | not built: "No automation tests matched" |

Read `tests/unit/[system]/` (or `integration/`) anywhere as the test root plus `[System]/`.

# Agent Coordination Rules

1. **Vertical Delegation**: Leadership agents delegate to department leads, who
   delegate to specialists. Never skip a tier for complex decisions.
2. **Horizontal Consultation**: Agents at the same tier may consult each other
   but must not make binding decisions outside their domain.
3. **Conflict Resolution**: When two agents disagree, escalate to the shared
   parent. If no shared parent, escalate to `creative-director` for design
   conflicts or `technical-director` for technical conflicts.
4. **Change Propagation**: When a design change affects multiple domains, the
   `producer` agent coordinates the propagation.
5. **No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes**: An agent must never modify files
   outside its designated directories without explicit delegation.
6. **Read Design Docs by Section**: A brief names the sections an agent needs
   by heading. Find a heading in a GDD, ADR or the art bible with the Grep
   tool (`^#`, content mode) and Read that range with offset and limit; read a doc
   whole only when the task needs all of it, and say why. `validate-read.sh`
   refuses a whole-file read of a doc over 40 KB.
7. **Nothing Goes Upstream**: Never file, open or comment on an issue or pull
   request in an engine, plugin or vendor repository, even when asked. Write a
   draft (`/bug-report` drafts only) and the user submits it.

## Model Tier Assignment

Read `.claude/docs/model-tiers.md` on demand. It carries the tier table, the
per-skill assignments and the authoring rule.

**Key point:** whether a skill's `model:` is used
depends on how the skill starts. Typed as `/skill-name`: yes, except a `haiku`
pin in auto mode. Started by Claude through the Skill tool: no. Never tell a
user a `haiku` skill saves money; an `opus` skill typed in a Sonnet session
costs more. The agent-side `model:` is a different mechanism, and is applied.

## Subagents vs Agent Teams

This project uses two distinct multi-agent patterns:

### Subagents (current, always active)
Spawned via the `Agent` tool within a single Claude Code session. Used by all
`team-*` skills and orchestration skills. Subagents share the session's
permission context, run sequentially or in parallel within the session, and
return results to the parent.

**When to spawn in parallel**: If two subagents' inputs are independent (neither
needs the other's output to begin), spawn both `Agent` calls simultaneously
rather than waiting. Example: `/review-all-gdds` **Phase 2** (consistency) and
**Phase 3** (design theory) are independent — spawn both at the same time.
Phase 1 loads the GDDs and both depend on it, so it is the one phase here that
must NOT be parallelised.

### Agent Teams (experimental — opt-in)
Multiple independent Claude Code *sessions* coordinated via a shared task list.
Opt-in only — read `.claude/docs/agent-teams.md` on demand before proposing one.

## Parallel Task Protocol

When an orchestration skill spawns multiple independent agents:

1. Issue all independent `Agent` calls before waiting for any result
2. Collect all results before proceeding to dependent phases
3. If any agent is BLOCKED, surface it immediately — do not silently skip
4. Always produce a partial report if some agents complete and others block

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
